successCriteria.description: A new Jest test file exists under tests/unit/modules/audit/ (a directory that does not exist today) and is discovered by the existing jest.config.js testMatch `**/tests/**/*.test.(ts|js)`; `npx jest` runs it green.
The phase's diff touches no file under src/ — `git diff --name-only` for the phase lists only files under tests/. Phases 1–3 are treated as fixed contracts.

PgAuditLogRepository.findByEntity is asserted to issue exactly one query through the injected fake pool, whose SQL selects from audit_logs with `WHERE entity_type = $1 AND entity_id = $2` and `ORDER BY occurred_at ASC, id ASC`, and whose parameter array is exactly [entityType, entityId] in that order.

Row mapping is asserted through the existing mapRow/parseState path: a JSON-string before_state/after_state column comes back as the parsed value, a null column comes back as null (not the string 'null', not undefined), and occurredAt is a Date instance.
A tie-break case is asserted: two rows sharing an identical occurredAt are returned in ascending id order, and a repeat call with the same input yields the same order (stability).

An empty result set from the fake pool resolves to [] and does not throw — asserted at the repository level and, separately, at the endpoint level as 200 with an empty array for an existing, visible request with no audit rows.
Via the Fastify route seam, the history endpoint returns 200 with the entries for the request's own employee, and a MANAGER reading a direct report's history also returns 200.

A requester who may not see the request receives the SAME 404 as a nonexistent id: both responses are asserted byte-identical (statusCode, body, and code 'NOT_FOUND'), and the invisible case is asserted never to be 403.

Each returned entry is asserted to carry exactly the keys { id, actorId, action, entityType, entityId, beforeState, afterState, occurredAt } — no added, renamed, or dropped field (e.g. an exact key-set comparison, not a partial matchObject).

constraints: No production source change: nothing under src/ may be modified, added, or deleted. Phases 1–3 (findByEntity/getByEntity, LeaveService.getHistory + LEAVE_REQUEST_ENTITY_TYPE, the GET /leaves/:id/history handler) are fixed contracts the tests assert against, not adjust.

In-memory fakes only — no jest.mock of the pg driver, no real Pool, no database connection. The repository is exercised by injecting a fake pool through the existing constructor seam `constructor(private readonly dbPool: Pool = defaultPool)`; the route is exercised by decorating the Fastify instance's `leaveService` seam, matching the existing suite.

Jest + ts-jest, TypeScript strict (no implicit any, strict null checks). HARNESS.json constraint `no-any` is enforced by CI lint: test doubles must be typed (e.g. `as unknown as ILeaveService` / `as unknown as Pool`), never `any`. Note tsconfig.json excludes `tests`, so ts-jest is the only typecheck gate these files pass through — they must compile under strict mode.

The tests must not assert implementation shape beyond the contract: no assertion on the exact whitespace/indentation of the SQL string, no assertion on the number of internal helper calls, no assertion that a specific private method exists. Assert the query's semantic content (table, WHERE predicate, ORDER BY, params) and the observable result.

The tests must not re-express the visibility rule. The route-level fake service may implement getById/getHistory for the seam, but no test may assert a role branch that the production code does not contain, and no test may assert a 403 from this endpoint.

The existing tests/unit/modules/leave/leave.routes.test.ts and tests/unit/modules/leave/leave.service.test.ts must keep passing unchanged in their existing cases; the extension is additive. The existing byte-identical-404 assertion pattern in leave.routes.test.ts is the pattern to mirror, not to replace.

The verification command runs `npm run build` (tsc --noEmit over src) and `npx jest --passWithNoTests --forceExit`; the new tests must pass under `--forceExit`, so no test may leave a handle open (close every Fastify instance in afterEach).

The phase must record its delivery in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md under the feature's "Audit trail for a single leave request" section (a "Phase 4 delivered" subsection), and correct the now-stale "Recommended phases" list which still shows Phases 2–4 as pending. The doc is the contract later features and the dependency check read.
outOfScope: Any change to src/ — including refactors, added exports, new helpers, or "testability" seams. The dbPool constructor seam and the fastify.leaveService decoration seam already exist and are sufficient.
Integration/e2e coverage against a real PostgreSQL instance, and any extension of scripts/smoke.js. This phase is Jest unit tests with in-memory fakes only.

Tests for the write path (create/submit/approve/reject/cancel audit recording), for AuditService.record/getById, and for the leave list/getById endpoints beyond what already exists — those are covered by the existing suites and are not this phase's subject.

Pagination, filtering, LIMIT/OFFSET, index extension, beforeState/afterState redaction, and occurred_at clock authority — all recorded as open questions in the feature's architecture section and deliberately unasserted here.
Asserting the GP-008 reversal trail semantics (a reversal row's own trail being empty) as a new test case; the empty-trail contract is covered generically by the empty-history criterion.

ambiguities.description: PLAN.md says the leave-side tests extend "the existing tests/unit/modules/leave/leave.routes.test.ts (or leave.service.test.ts)" — the file is not fixed. The route seam is the only place the endpoint visibility and byte-identical-404 criteria can be asserted, so the routes file is the natural home; the service file would only cover getHistory's delegation.
options: Extend leave.routes.test.ts only (route seam covers all three endpoint criteria)
Extend leave.routes.test.ts for endpoint criteria AND add getHistory delegation cases to leave.service.test.ts

ambiguities.description: The new audit test file's scope is stated as the entity-query ordering/mapping/tie-break/empty-result behaviour of PgAuditLogRepository.findByEntity. It is unstated whether it should also cover AuditService.getByEntity (its ValidationError on empty entityType/entityId, and its verbatim passthrough of an empty array) — the existing tests/unit/modules/audit.service.test.ts has no getByEntity cases at all, so that behaviour is currently unasserted anywhere.
options: Repository-level findByEntity only, as the plan enumerates
Repository-level findByEntity plus AuditService.getByEntity validation and empty-array passthrough

ambiguities.description: The tie-break criterion says two rows with an identical occurredAt come back in ascending id order. With a fake pool the repository returns whatever the fake yields, so the assertion can only verify that the repository does not re-sort and that the SQL carries the `id ASC` tie-break — it cannot prove PostgreSQL's ordering. Whether the test should additionally assert the SQL text contains the tie-break clause (rather than only the returned order) is unstated.
options: Assert both the SQL tie-break clause and the returned order/stability
Assert returned order and stability only

ambiguities.description: The endpoint-visibility criterion requires a MANAGER reading a direct report's history to return 200. The route-level fake service must therefore encode the manager/report relationship. Whether the fake should mirror the production getById rule (visibleIds = [actor.id, ...reports]) or simply return entries for the requested id is unstated; the former risks the test asserting the fake rather than the route.
options: Fake mirrors the production visibility rule (as the existing buildApp fake does)
Fake returns entries unconditionally and the test asserts only the route's pass-through of 200
Drive the real LeaveService with fake repositories instead of a fake service

entityInvariants.invariant: Lifecycle RECORDED — terminal and immutable; reached once at insert. The tests must treat an entry as read-only data: no test may assert an update, delete, or re-record path, and the mapped entry must be structurally identical to what findById already returns (same eight fields, beforeState/afterState as parsed `unknown | null`, occurredAt as a Date).

Lifecycle EMPTY | POPULATED, with no error state. EMPTY (entity visible, zero matching rows) is a successful 200-with-[] outcome, never 404 and never a throw; POPULATED is one or more entries ordered occurredAt ASC then id ASC. NOTE — residual inconsistency: .gestalt/architecture/reconciled.json still declares AuditTrail with `entries`/`entryCount`, but Phase 2 delivered no AuditTrail type (getHistory returns the audit-owned AuditLog[] directly). docs/ARCHITECTURE.md records this divergence as resolved in favour of the code; the tests must assert the built shape (a bare array), not the reconciled wrapper.

Lifecycle DRAFT | SUBMITTED | APPROVED | REJECTED | CANCELLED, unchanged by this feature. The history read is visibility-gated by the request's existence and the caller's relationship to it, not by its status: a request in any status that the caller may see yields its trail (or an empty one), and a request the caller may not see yields the same 404 as a nonexistent id regardless of status.

interfaceConstraints.operation: IAuditRepository.findByEntity(entityType, entityId) — the entity-scoped trail read
interfaceConstraints.authRule: None. The audit module is role-blind and must stay so: no EmployeeRole import, no role branch, no authorization. Visibility is owned by the leave module.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns AuditLog[] — possibly empty, never null, never throws on zero matching rows. Takes NO optional trailing PoolClient (the read path opens no transaction and joins none). Ordering is owned by the repository's SQL (occurred_at ASC, id ASC); no caller may re-sort. The tests must assert this signature and behaviour as built.

interfaceConstraints.operation: IAuditService.getByEntity(entityType, entityId) — the service-level trail read
interfaceConstraints.authRule: None — no role check, no EmployeeRole branch.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: ValidationError (400, code VALIDATION_ERROR) for a non-string or whitespace-only entityType/entityId, with the repository NOT reached; otherwise the repository's array returned verbatim, including an empty array — never NotFoundError for an empty trail. No PoolClient parameter.

interfaceConstraints.operation: ILeaveService.getHistory(actor, requestId) — the leave-owned trail read
interfaceConstraints.authRule: Authorization is exactly the existing getById(actor, requestId) visibility rule (ADMIN sees all; MANAGER sees own plus direct reports, one level; anyone else only own), called FIRST and allowed to throw. It must not be re-expressed, and the method must not branch on EmployeeRole.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: NotFoundError (404, code NOT_FOUND) propagated unchanged from getById for both an invisible and a nonexistent request — byte-identical, never 403. A visible request with zero audit rows returns [] (200), never NotFoundError. Read-only: no uow.withTransaction, no PoolClient accepted or forwarded, no writes.

interfaceConstraints.operation: GET /leaves/:id/history — the HTTP trail read (asserted, not built)
interfaceConstraints.authRule: Authentication via the existing registerAuth preHandler populating request.user; the route's existing resolveActor helper enforces id presence and EmployeeRole membership (401 UnauthorizedError otherwise). No role guard and no EmployeeRole branch in the route — authorization is entirely the service's getById call.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: 200 with the AuditLog[] array verbatim (oldest first, no wrapper, no re-sort, no mapping, no filter, no cap); 200 with [] for an existing visible request with no rows; 404 { error, code: 'NOT_FOUND' } byte-identical for an invisible and a nonexistent id; 401 for a missing/invalid actor; 500 via sendError for a non-AppError throw. 403 is never produced by this endpoint.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The repository test must inject its fake pool through the EXISTING constructor seam `constructor(private readonly dbPool: Pool = defaultPool)` and assert the query issued through the private `db(client?)` accessor with no client argument — do not add a seam, do not jest.mock the pg module.

The mapping assertions must target the existing mapRow/parseState behaviour (JSON column -> parsed value, null column -> null, occurred_at -> Date) and the existing COLUMNS constant — the test must not re-implement or duplicate the mapping, and must not assert a json/jsonb column type (before_state/after_state are TEXT holding JSON strings).

The route tests must reuse the existing Fastify buildApp pattern: decorate the instance's `leaveService` seam with an in-memory ILeaveService fake, `decorateRequest('user', undefined)` plus a preHandler hook setting request.user, `app.register(leaveRoutes)`, `app.ready()`, `app.inject(...)`, and `app.close()` in afterEach. Mirror the existing byte-identical-404 assertion (`expect(invisible.json()).toEqual(missing.json())`).

The leave-side fake service must satisfy the current ILeaveService interface (which now includes getHistory) and be typed via `as unknown as ILeaveService`, matching the existing suite's convention — not `any` (HARNESS.json `no-any`).

The audit-side fake repository must satisfy the current IAuditRepository (create, findById, findByEntity) so it typechecks under ts-jest strict mode, matching the existing FakeAuditRepository in the audit service suite.

The response-field assertion must match the audit-owned AuditLog entity exactly — the eight fields { id, actorId, action, entityType, entityId, beforeState, afterState, occurredAt } — imported from the audit module's public entry point, with no leave-owned projection or DTO introduced.

The 404 body assertion must match the existing sendError contract: `{ error: string, code: string }` with NotFoundError producing statusCode 404 and code 'NOT_FOUND' — assert the code, not a hardcoded message string.

integrationPoints.target: src/modules/audit/audit.repository.ts — PgAuditLogRepository constructor dbPool seam and the private db(client?) accessor
integrationPoints.why: The only way to observe the entity-scoped SQL and its params without a database; the fake pool is injected here.

integrationPoints.target: src/modules/leave/leave.routes.ts — the fastify.leaveService decoration seam and the leaveRoutes(fastify) registration
integrationPoints.why: The route-level visibility, byte-identical-404, empty-history, and response-field criteria are only assertable through this seam.

integrationPoints.target: tests/unit/modules/leave/leave.routes.test.ts — the existing buildApp helper, actor preHandler hook, and byte-identical-404 assertion
integrationPoints.why: The extension must be additive to this file and reuse its established pattern rather than introduce a second harness.

integrationPoints.why: The new file under tests/unit/modules/audit/ is only discovered if it matches this pattern; ts-jest is the sole typecheck gate for tests since tsconfig.json excludes tests.

integrationPoints.target: src/modules/audit/index.ts — the public entry point exporting AuditLog, IAuditRepository, PgAuditLogRepository, IAuditService, AuditService

The entity discriminator the trail is keyed by; the tests' fixture entityType must use this constant so a writer/reader literal divergence cannot hide behind a matching hardcoded string.
